id: title:jose-sequeira:scope taxonomy suggestion similarity to the project

review.posthog_relevance: Changes the implementation of name similarity matching in the taxonomy module, potentially reducing database load by avoiding global GIN index scans and allowing PostHog to control similarity thresholds.
review.reason: Adds a module-level constant for trigram similarity and replaces database-side GIN index lookups with Python-side annotations and filtering. This could reduce database load and allow PostHog to control similarity thresholds, though exact performance and correctness implications depend on database state.
review.uncertainty: Exact performance and correctness implications depend on database state and are not demonstrated; potential benefit is conjectured rather than proven.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No score assigned; tier requires assessment.

observations.behavior: Adds a module-level constant TRIGRAM_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.3 and documentation explaining its relationship to pg_trgm defaults.
observations.posthog_connection: Makes the similarity threshold an explicit Python constant rather than relying on Postgres server configuration, allowing PostHog to control the cutoff for name suggestions regardless of database settings.

observations.behavior: Replaces the use of the database-level `name__trigram_similar` lookup with a Python-side `TrigramSimilarity` annotation and explicit filtering, while retaining exact matches for dollar-prefixed names.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes the implementation of name similarity matching from a database-side GIN index lookup to a Python-side annotation and filter. This could reduce database load by avoiding the global GIN index scan and applying the similarity threshold and exact match filtering after the initial annotation, though the exact performance and correctness implications depend on the database state.
